nodes.title: A parse result, not an exception
nodes.why: Typing produces invalid JSON on most keystrokes. Catching the error and returning it as a value lets the screen show a message instead of crashing the tree.
nodes.alternative: Call `JSON.parse` in render without a try.
nodes.tradeoff: An uncaught error unmounts the whole component tree on the first stray comma.

nodes.title: One component that calls itself

anchor.snippet: function JsonNode({ name, value, path, collapsed, onToggle }: NodeProps) {

nodes.why: A JSON value is a tree of the same shape at every level, so one component that renders an entry and then its children handles any depth.
nodes.alternative: Flatten the tree into rows with a depth and render a list.
nodes.tradeoff: Flat rows make virtualising large values easy, but collapsing has to skip a node's descendants by hand.

nodes.title: Let JSON write the primitives
nodes.why: `JSON.stringify` quotes and escapes strings and writes numbers, booleans and `null` exactly as the input did, so the tree reads like the text it came from.
nodes.alternative: Wrap strings in quotes with a template literal.
nodes.tradeoff: A hand-made quote misses escapes: a string with a quote or a newline would read differently from its JSON.

nodes.title: State keyed by path
nodes.why: A path names the same node however the text around it changes, so a collapsed `$.owner` stays collapsed when a sibling key is added.
nodes.alternative: Keep an `open` state inside each node component.
nodes.tradeoff: Local state works while React keeps the component, but a parse error unmounts the tree and every node opens again when the text is fixed.

nodes.title: Empty containers have nothing to toggle
nodes.why: A toggle that opens nothing is noise for sighted and screen reader users alike, so an empty container renders as its value.
nodes.alternative: Render every container the same way, with a toggle.
nodes.tradeoff: Uniform code, but `[…] 0 items` behind a button reads as content that is not there.
